notes:
Summary: Firespan is evaluating a RAG-based deflection + agent assist stack. They have ~60M historical ticket rows, expect to index ~120M vectors (combined ticket segments + KB), estimated raw vector store size ~350GB before quantization. Primary goals: 1) deflect up to 35% of inbound tickets via self-serve, 2) high-quality top-5 rerank for agent suggestions, 3) strict latency SLOs for end-to-end retrieval+rerank < 200ms p50, target p95 < 400ms under steady-state load.

Workload specifics:
- Query traffic baseline: 25–50 qps during peak for search endpoint; 150 qps aggregated across async embedding jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per user query (retrieval + rerank) < $0.03 — current in-house prototype at ~$0.09.
- Retrieval: dense embeddings + approximate nearest neighbors (ANN), cold cache hit-rate low (org-wide).
- Reranking: require cross-encoder-style reranker for top-5 precision; acceptable to run reranker on small GPU pool but must finish <50ms ideally.
- Embedding model: prefer open/small-cost models (instruction-tuned, 1536–3072 dim) but willing to test Redwood-verified models for cost/quality tradeoffs.

Security & deployment:
- Must support VPC private deployment or on-prem air-gapped option for EU customer subsets.
- Data residency: EU for EU customers; global controls required.
- Must pass SOC2 & SSO/SAML + KMS integration and provide audit logs for query-level access.

POC asks & success criteria:
- 6-week POC: ingest 1M prioritized tickets + KB, run A/B with in-house ranker for top-5 precision and latency.
- Performance targets: p50 retrieval+rerank <200ms, p95 <400ms at 25 qps; reranker cost per query < $0.02 (target).
- Indexing scale test: demonstrate 120M-vector index performance with quantization recommendations; show storage reduction and latency impact.
- Quality: achieve >8% absolute improvement in top-5 deflection rate vs baseline (measured on labeled holdout set).

Quotes/snippets from call:
- "We need the reranker to be invisible to users — quality over flashy LLM answers."
- "If you can hit p95 <400ms and bring cost down, procurement will move fast."

Open items / blockers:
- Legal needs a DPA + data flow diagram for EU residency.
- Product team needs clarification on what counts toward the latency SLO (retrieval, rerank, model scoring).
- Procurement expects 60–90 day lead time for Dedicated capacity unless Private packaging is chosen.

Recommended Redwood approach (SE notes):
- Start POC on Dedicated with a small GPU reranker pool (multi-tenant but reserved for POC), enable prefix/KV caching for hot tickets, run Redwood Optimize to pick embedding dims and quantization strategy, run a short stress test demonstrating p95 at target qps.
- Provide a short benchmarking report (tokenized latency, bytes / vector, cost per query scenarios) and a checklist for legal (SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration steps, DPA draft).
